 If Micron Grows At 10% a Year, Here’s What $1,000 Becomes By 2030
 Micron just posted explosive revenue growth and locked in contracts stretching toward 2030, yet the stock tumbled hard last week. Whether that pullback is a buying opportunity or a warning sign depends entirely on which scenario plays out for your…
 By Vandita Jadeja 
 Published October 21, 2026, 12:30pm ET · 3 min read 
 Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja .

 Quick Read
 Micron's base-case model projects 48% returns over five years, with the bull case delivering $2,684 from a $1,000 investment by 2031.
 Micron is developing the industry's first custom HBM4E implementation with NVIDIA, while 26 long-term contracts lock in 35% of revenue through 2030.

 Micron Technology ( NASDAQ:MU | MU Price Prediction ) closed at $878.84 after a 14.58% one-week decline. That pullback raises a simple question: if you put $1,000 into the memory maker today, what could that investment be worth by 2030?
 The stock deserves a forward look because Micron just reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $133.19B, up 256.3% year over year.
 What $1,000 in Micron Could Become
 Our model’s nearest horizon to 2030 is the five-year target. In the base case, a $1,000 investment could be worth about $1,487.40 by 2031, a total return of 48.74%. That rests on a base-case share price of $1,307.18 on October 17, 2031, or 8.26% annualized.
 For 2030 itself (an example point on the path, not a separately projected horizon), the base-case path puts shares at $1,287.27 in October 2030. That would turn $1,000 into about $1,464.74.
 Compare that with the basic math: $1,000 compounding at 10% a year for four years becomes $1,464.10. The model’s base path and the 10% hook land almost in the same spot.

 On the example October 2030 date, the bull path hits $2,161.07 per share and the bear path $711.94. Over one year, the model targets $985.43 (+12.13%), with a bull case of $1,347.86 and a bear case of $741.69. The model’s confidence rating is 0.9, rated high.
 Wall Street is more aggressive. The analyst consensus target is $1,560.57, with 9 Strong Buy, 36 Buy, 3 Hold and 1 Strong Sell rating. 
 24/7 Wall St. 
 Three Drivers Behind the Upside Case
 Demand Still Outrunning Supply
 Management sees no near-term balance. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said on the fiscal Q4 call, “In calendar year 27 as well as 2028, we see demand exceeding supply.” 
 The company added that “more than 75% of our output is already committed for 2027.” Micron is also working with NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) on “the industry’s first custom HBM4E implementation”.
 Contracts That Reach Toward 2030
 Micron has signed 26 strategic customer agreements, which management estimates cover over 35% of revenue through 2030. All include take-or-pay volumes, and remaining performance obligations stand near $150 billion.
 That visibility ties Micron directly to the AI data-center expansion (we highlighted seven non-chip suppliers riding the same wave, from power to cooling, in a report available at no cost here ). For a five-year holder, that locked-in demand matters more than any single quarter.
 Earnings Momentum
 Fiscal Q4 revenue hit $54.23B, up 379.3%, and non-GAAP EPS of $33.42 exceeded the $31.35 estimate. Fiscal Q1 2027 guidance calls for $61.5B ± $1.5B in revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $38.15 ± $1.00.
 Risks That Could Shrink Your $1,000
 Memory is historically cyclical , and today’s record margins (87.0% non-GAAP gross margin in fiscal Q4) leave little room for upside surprises if pricing turns. The model’s forward P/E component prices the stock at only $436.41, a sign the market may be discounting peak-cycle earnings.
 Spending is heavy: capex reached $30.7B in fiscal 2026, and first-half fiscal 2027 capex is expected near $25 billion. Labor tension is another wildcard, as Taiwan’s president urged Micron and workers to negotiate sincerely ahead of a possible strike (Reuters). With a beta of 2.226, moves will be sharp. A downside outcome would leave $1,000 at $849.
 Where Your $1,000 Could Land
 Across the five-year model, a $1,000 Micron investment ranges from about $849 in the bear case to $2,684.40 in the bull case, with a base case of $1,487.40.
 The example 2030 base path of $1,464.74 tracks the 10% a year basic closely. These are scenarios, not guarantees. This is a projection, not investment advice.
